Vivek / team — quick read and recommendations.

Summary of risk: Acme is asking for a typical provider IP indemnity (defend & indemnify for third-party IP claims). That's reasonable but we need to: (1) tightly define scope to Redwood-delivered services and our pre-trained models as provided; (2) carve out Customer Content, Customer Modifications, data they upload, and any third-party models/components where Acme is responsible; (3) preserve defense control for Redwood but require we keep Acme reasonably informed and obtain consent for settlements that bind Acme.

Suggested redlines (high-level):
- Scope: "Provider Indemnity" limited to claims that use of the unmodified Service or Provider Software as provided infringes a third party's patents, copyrights or trade secrets. Exclude claims to the extent arising from: (a) Customer Content; (b) Customer Configurations or Modifications; (c) combination of the Service with Customer systems not reasonably anticipated by Provider; (d) open-source components as identified in Appendix X.
- Defense / Settlement Control: Provider shall have the right to assume and control the defense with counsel of its choosing; Provider shall not settle any claim that imposes ongoing liability or injunctive relief on Customer without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Customer must cooperate and may participate at its own expense.
- Remedies: primary obligation to (i) procure the right to continue providing the Service; or (ii) replace or modify the Service to avoid infringement; failing that, refund of fees paid for the affected Service during the 12 months prior to the claim. No open-ended consequential damages.
- Cap carveout: propose an explicit carveout from the general monetary cap for IP indemnity up to a fixed cap (suggest $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees, whichever is greater) OR alternatively we can offer no cap but limit to replacement/repair/refund only. Commercial should weigh which is acceptable.
- Insurance: ask Acme to represent they maintain Cyber/GL insurance and confirm carrier/limits for large deals.

Why these positions? They protect Redwood operationally (defense control, reasonable settlement consent) while giving Customer meaningful remedies (repair/replace/refund). Pure unlimited indemnities or defense/control forfeits are too risky for platform vendors.

Action items:
- Karthik / Marissa: advise if a $1M IP carveout or 12 months fees (we can default to whichever is greater) would be a deal-killer.
- Vivek: if Commercial prefers refund-only remedy, we'll prepare language that limits monetary liability and offers refund/replace as sole remedy.

I'll prepare proposed redline language and attach.

Emma — thanks for the clear redlines and for the patience while we reviewed internally. We discussed commercial trade-offs and Redwood's legal position. Below is a compromise proposal intended to be signable for both sides; attached are two short redlines (MSA excerpt + Order Form paragraph).

What Redwood can commit to:
- Provider IP Indemnity: Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims that the unmodified Redwood Service or Provider Software, as delivered by Redwood, infringes a third party's patent, copyright or trade secret.
- Scope carveouts: the indemnity expressly excludes any claim arising from (i) Customer Content; (ii) Customer Modifications or integrations; (iii) third-party models or components incorporated by Customer; and (iv) open-source components listed in Exhibit A.
- Defense & Settlement: Redwood may assume and control the defense with counsel of its choosing. Redwood will consult with Customer and will not enter into any settlement that imposes monetary or non-monetary obligations on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld for monetary settlements up to the indemnity cap).
- Remedies & Cap: Redwood's obligation will be to (in order of preference) (a) procure the right to continue providing the Service; (b) replace or modify the Service to avoid infringement; and if neither is commercially reasonable, (c) refund fees paid for the affected Service in the 12 months prior to the claim. The IP indemnity will be subject to a monetary cap equal to the greater of (i) USD $1,000,000 or (ii) twelve (12) months of Fees paid by Customer under the Orders giving rise to the claim.
- Customer Indemnity (reciprocal): Customer will indemnify Redwood for claims arising out of Customer Content, Customer Modifications, Customer-provided data, or Customer's misuse of the Service.

We believe this preserves meaningful protection for Acme while keeping Redwood's exposure bounded. If Acme prefers to remove the monetary cap in exchange for limiting remedies to repair/replace only, we can discuss that alternative.

Next steps: attached are the redlined MSA excerpt and a short Order Form amendment that implements the language above. If Acme can confirm acceptance of these points, we'll prepare an e-signature packet for execution. Happy to set a 20-minute call with Neha to walk through the legal points if helpful.

Best,
